title: The middle extension does not change the $L^2$-weight
statement:
Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion
with finite complement $S_0$, and let $\mathcal M$ be a nonzero lisse
Weil sheaf of rank $r$ on $U_0$, punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $w$. Write $\|f_{\mathcal M}\|_m^2$ for
the sum of squares of the trace function of $\mathcal M$ over
$U_0(k_m)$ as in [def-wf-l2-norm], and
$\|f_{j_*\mathcal M}\|_m^2$ for the same sum for the
middle extension over
$\mathbf A^1_{k_0}(k_m)$. Then the two parameters that these sums
define through the ratio of [def-wf-l2-norm] coincide, and equal
$w$:

$$
\|j_*\mathcal M\|=\|\mathcal M\|=w .
$$

proof.text: The open $U_0$ is a smooth geometrically connected affine curve: it is the principal open obtained by inverting the product of the irreducible polynomials defining the finitely many points of $S_0$ (the empty product is $1$), and after extending the field it is a nonempty open of the irreducible affine line. Its lisse sheaf $\mathcal M$ is nonzero by hypothesis, hence its constant rank is $r\ge1$. Apply [lem-wf-l2-purity-rigidity] to this curve and sheaf, obtaining $\|\mathcal M\|=w$.

Put $a_m=\|f_{\mathcal M}\|_m^2$ and $b_m=\|f_{j_*\mathcal M}\|_m^2$ for $m\ge1$, using [def-wf-l2-norm]. For an etale test scheme $V$ over $U_0$, the section formula of [def-wf-middle-extension] gives $(j_*\mathcal M)(V)=\mathcal M(V\times_{\mathbf A^1}U_0)=\mathcal M(V)$, with the same restrictions and Weil maps. Thus the stalk traces agree over $U_0$. Partitioning the finite set of rational points into the open and its complement gives
$$b_m=a_m+E_m,\qquad E_m=\sum_{y\in S_0(k_m)}|\iota t_{j_*\mathcal M}(y)|^2\ge0.$$
This is an equality for ordinary sheaf direct image, not for $Rj_*$.

For $s\in S_0$ let $d_s=[\kappa(s):k_0]$ and $V_s=(j_*\mathcal M)_{\bar s}$. By [lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants], $V_s$ is the inertia-invariant subspace of the rank-$r$ local generic stalk; hence $n_s:=\dim V_s\le r$. By [def-weil-punctual-weights], purity gives $|\iota\alpha|^2=q_x^w$ for every closed-point eigenvalue on $U_0$. The hypotheses of [lem-wf-boundary-semicontinuity] therefore hold with $\beta=w$ on the smooth geometrically connected curve $\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$, with $r\ge1$. Its conclusion gives $|\iota\alpha|^2\le q_s^w=q^{d_sw}$ for every eigenvalue of $F_s$ on $V_s$.

Apply the point-count identity of [prop-euler-product] to the reduced finite $k_0$-scheme $S_0$. If $c_d$ counts its degree-$d$ closed points, then
$$\#S_0(k_m)=\sum_{d\mid m}d c_d\le\sum_{s\in S_0}d_s=:D.$$
In particular a rational point $y$ over $s$ can occur only if $d_s\mid m$: the residue-field map $\kappa(s)\hookrightarrow k_m$ makes $m$ a multiple of $d_s$ by the degree formula for a tower of finite fields. When $S_0$ is empty, $D=0$.

Restrict to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. By [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus], represent the underlying object, Weil isomorphism, inverse and inverse identities at one finite coefficient stage $E$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. On each geometric component, the point equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] identifies this sheaf with its finite-dimensional $E$-space. Choose a basis and the lattice $\mathcal O_E^{n_s}$ there, using completed integral coefficients. Its reductions are finite free in degree zero, hence bounded constructible of finite Tor dimension. These choices provide an integral representative of the underlying object; no Frobenius-stable lattice is needed.

For $y\in S_0(k_m)$ above $s$, apply [lem-trf-rational-local-frobenius-powers] to obtain conjugacy of its normalized operator with $F_s^{m/d_s}$. This is also the operator of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]: [lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization] identifies the successive point transport $t_{y,m}$ with the specified scheme-Frobenius transport $J_y(\kappa^{(m)})\rho_{y,m}$ at the rational stage. Postcomposition with the pulled-back iterated Weil map therefore gives the same local operator. Restriction uses the same point and Weil iterates, so computes the original boundary stalk. The normalization lemma also supplies coefficient coherence. Extending the conjugacy from $E$ to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ preserves composition and inverse; thus $F_y^{(m)}$ on the original stalk is conjugate to $F_s^{m/d_s}$.

Over the algebraically closed field $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use [p-linear-triangular] on $F_s$ and choose a basis adapted to its invariant full flag. Its matrix is upper triangular, with diagonal $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_{n_s}$; these are its eigenvalues, since its characteristic polynomial is the product of $T-\alpha_i$. For upper triangular matrices $A,B$, $(AB)_{ii}=A_{ii}B_{ii}$, since a nonzero term $A_{ij}B_{ji}$ forces both $i\le j$ and $j\le i$. Induction therefore gives diagonal entries $\alpha_i^{m/d_s}$ for $F_s^{m/d_s}$. The basis-independent trace of [def-weil-endomorphism-trace] and Step 5 yield
$$|\iota t_{j_*\mathcal M}(y)|=\left|\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\iota(\alpha_i)^{m/d_s}\right|\le\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}|\iota(\alpha_i)|^{m/d_s}\le r q^{mw/2}.$$
Here Step 3 gives each summand at most $(q^{d_sw/2})^{m/d_s}=q^{mw/2}$; no semisimplicity is used. Squaring and using Step 4 in the sum of Step 2 proves
$$0\le E_m\le D r^2 q^{mw}=:Cq^{mw}.$$
The zero-dimensional stalk has an empty sum and satisfies the same bound.

Use the supremum definition [def-wf-l2-norm]. Since $a_m\le b_m$, positivity of the limit superior of $a_m/q^{m(\beta+1)}$ implies positivity for $b_m/q^{m(\beta+1)}$. Inclusion of these parameter sets gives $\|j_*\mathcal M\|\ge\|\mathcal M\|=w$. For the reverse bound fix any real $\beta>w$. Step 1 and the definition of supremum imply that the nonnegative sequence $a_m/q^{m(\beta+1)}$ has limit superior zero (a positive limit superior would put $\beta$ in a set with supremum $w$), so it tends to zero. Steps 2 and 6 give
$$0\le\frac{b_m}{q^{m(\beta+1)}}\le\frac{a_m}{q^{m(\beta+1)}}+Cq^{m(w-\beta-1)}.$$
The final term tends to zero because $q>1$ and $w-\beta-1<0$: it is $C\rho^m$ with $0<\rho=q^{w-\beta-1}<1$. Hence the middle sequence tends to zero by the elementary squeeze argument. No parameter greater than $w$ belongs to its positive-limsup set, whose supremum is therefore at most $w$. Together the bounds give $\|j_*\mathcal M\|=\|\mathcal M\|=w$.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion
with finite complement $S_0$, and let $\mathcal M$ be a nonzero lisse
Weil sheaf of rank $r$ on $U_0$, punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $w$. Write $\|f_{\mathcal M}\|_m^2$ for
the sum of squares of the trace function of $\mathcal M$ over
$U_0(k_m)$ as in [def-wf-l2-norm], and
$\|f_{j_*\mathcal M}\|_m^2$ for the same sum for the
middle extension over
$\mathbf A^1_{k_0}(k_m)$. Then the two parameters that these sums
define through the ratio of [def-wf-l2-norm] coincide, and equal
$w$:

$$
\|j_*\mathcal M\|=\|\mathcal M\|=w .
$$

proof.text:
The rigidity [lem-wf-l2-purity-rigidity] gives
$\|\mathcal M\|=w$ directly. For the comparison, the two sums agree
on $U_0(k_m)$, so

$$
\|f_{j_*\mathcal M}\|_m^2=\|f_{\mathcal M}\|_m^2+E_m,
\qquad
E_m=\sum_{y\in S_0(k_m)}\bigl|t_{j_*\mathcal M}(y)\bigr|^2\ge0 .
$$

Since $S_0$ is finite, $\#S_0(k_m)\le D:=\sum_{s\in S_0}d(s)$ for
every $m$; and at $y\in S_0(k_m)$ lying above the closed point
$s\in S_0$, the local Frobenius $F_y$ has the eigenvalues
$\alpha^{m/d(s)}$ for $\alpha$ running over the eigenvalues of
$F_s$ on the boundary stalk of the middle extension, which by the
boundary semicontinuity [lem-wf-boundary-semicontinuity] — applied
to $\mathcal M$ with $\beta=w$, the punctual purity of
[def-weil-punctual-weights] exhibiting $\mathcal M$ as punctually
mixed of weights at most $w$ — satisfy
$|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q_s^{w}=q^{d(s)w}$. Hence
$|\iota(\alpha^{m/d(s)})|^2\le q^{mw}$ and

$$
E_m\le D\,r^2q^{mw}=C\,q^{mw}
$$

for every $m$, with the constant $C:=D\,r^2$.

Now $\|f_{\mathcal M}\|_m^2\le\|f_{j_*\mathcal M}\|_m^2$ for every
$m$, so every parameter with a positive limit superior for
$\mathcal M$ has one for $j_*\mathcal M$ as well: this gives
$\|j_*\mathcal M\|\ge\|\mathcal M\|$. Conversely, for $\beta>w$ the
ratio of [def-wf-l2-norm] for $j_*\mathcal M$ is bounded by the
ratio for $\mathcal M$, which has limit superior $0$ because
$\beta>\|\mathcal M\|$, plus $Cq^{m(w-\beta-1)}$, which also has
limit superior $0$ because $\beta+1>w$. No $\beta>w$ therefore has
a positive limit superior, so $\|j_*\mathcal M\|\le w$, and the two
parameters agree and equal $w$.
